review_summary: Independent review of draft.xlsx (Datalink/Insight, DEFM14A dated 11/29/2016) against instruction v1.13.2. The ledger is careful overall. All 67 quotations match the filing verbatim at the cited pages, flags and Questions cross-reference exactly, and the process/round map, exits, re-entries and deadline outcomes follow the text. Eleven candidate findings: four clear existing-rule errors (F1 exact did-not-submit counts that fail Part B's subtraction test; F2 cohort Type Unknown despite a stated strategic/financial split, plus a sort-order slip; F4 Conditions Light on Insight's November bids while diligence was open; F5 All cash Yes on a price-only bid), one omission (F3 Insight's NDA dated 06/14/2016 in Annex A), and six convention-dependent points (F6 Party A's March proposal counted as a round-2 IOI with no round-2 row; F7 Party C's reaffirmation as a Bid vs E10; F8 Party C's exit date and reason; F9 round-1 opening; F10 Insight's added closing conditions; F11 Projections given to Insight). No omitted bid, exit, deadline or round was found. This review does not establish that the ledger is complete.
read_scope: All four workbook sheets, every row and cell
Background of the Merger, pp. 27–35, in full and in order
Reasons for the Board's Recommendation, pp. 35–39 (incl. p.36: 27 bidders/23 NDAs; 'submit and affirm best and final')
Certain Datalink Unaudited Prospective Financial Information, opening passage pp. 39–40
Parties to the merger, p.19; cover page (filing dated 11/29/2016)
Opinion of Datalink's Financial Advisor: materials-reviewed passage (p.42) and fee paragraph (pp.47–48)
Financing of the Merger (p.48); Voting Agreement paragraph in the interests section (p.51); 7.0% voting-agreement figure (p.78)
Merger Agreement summary: consideration (p.62); No Solicitation (pp.68–69)
Annex A merger agreement: Section 5.6 access/confidentiality (p. A-32), found by keyword search for confidentiality-agreement dates
limitations: I read the filing as HTML converted to text. Page numbers come from the printed page footers, so a passage near a page break could be off by one page. Every quotation cited here was checked against that page mapping.

Annex A (merger agreement), Annex D (opinion letter), the valuation analyses, the interests section and the litigation and dissenters' rights material were searched by keyword and spot-read, not read line by line. An event disclosed only there could have been missed.
The bidders' identities (Party A/B/C and the unnamed parties) were not investigated, as instructed.
This single-reviewer check against the instruction does not prove the ledger complete. Several findings (F6–F11) depend on conventions the research team must decide.
Workbook formatting was checked only for freeze panes, filters and date formats. Text wrap and fonts were not audited.

findings.claim: The exact Counts on the two round-2 'Did not submit' cohorts (5 strategic, 8 financial) break Part B's subtraction test. The filing never establishes that the unnamed IOI submitters were among the NDA signers.
findings.current_workbook: #24 (Excel row 25) Count 5 = 10 strategic NDA signers − Party A − Insight − Party B − 2 unnamed strategic submitters. #28 (Excel row 29) Count 8 = 13 financial signers − Party C − 4 unnamed financial submitters. Q5 recommends keeping both counts exact. Rounds round 2 'How it ended' says 'thirteen did not submit'.

evidence.quote: 10 of which (including Party A, Party B and Insight) signed a non-disclosure agreement
five financial sponsors, including Party C, submitted initial indications of interest
Raymond James also communicated to the interested parties that initial indications of interest were due

rules: B (subtraction exact only when every party subtracted is an established member of the total)
E3 Counts
E14 Did not submit ('a range where a submitter's membership is uncertain')
F check 3
findings.proposed_correction: Blank Count on #24 and #28. Begin the Notes 'Count: 5–7' (strategic: 10 − Party A, Insight, Party B − 0 to 2 unnamed submitters that are established signers) and 'Count: 8–9' (financial: 13 − Party C − 3 to 4, since only one of the 14 sponsors did not sign). Change Rounds round 2 'How it ended' to 'thirteen to sixteen did not submit'. Update Q5's recommendation to match.
findings.reasoning: Only Party A, Insight, Party B and Party C are named as both signers and submitters. The two unnamed strategic and four unnamed financial submitters are not established signers. Three strategic and one financial contacted parties declined NDAs, and a submitter could be one of them. The draft states this assumption in Q5 but still records exact integers. Part B says that exactness misleads the model's count of live bidders and non-submitters (use 1) as much as an invented number would.

findings.claim: The six-member 'other IOI submitters' cohort has Type Unknown even though the filing gives its split (2 strategic, 4 financial). It is also sorted 07/21, so the two strategic IOIs sit after the 07/18 strategic deadline and the strategic did-not-submit row they answered.
findings.current_workbook: #26 (Excel row 27) Who '6 other IOI submitters (2 strategic, 4 financial)', Type Unknown, Count 6, Price $8.80–$10.50, Sort date 07/21/2016, placed after #23 Deadline 07/18 and #24.

evidence.quote: Four strategic parties (in addition to Party A, which submitted the proposal described above on March 29, 2016), including Insight and Party B
The other initial indications of interest included prices from a low of $8.80 per share to a high of $10.50 per share.
initial indications of interest were due on July 18, 2016 from strategic buyers and July 21, 2016 from financial sponsors

rules: E3 Cohorts ('split by type only where the filing gives the split'; Unknown only for an unsplit population)
E8 Sort date (due date for a response with no arrival day)
E13 (a group range belongs on that group's cohort row only)
findings.proposed_correction: Split into '2 other strategic IOI submitters' (Strategic, Count 2, Sort 07/18/2016, placed with #21–#22 before #23) and '4 other financial IOI submitters' (Financial, Count 4, Sort 07/21/2016). For the $8.80–$10.50 range, either leave the price cells blank on both rows and quote the range in each Note, or keep the range only on one combined price-bearing row. E13 ties a group range to 'that group's cohort row', so which option to use is a convention call to raise in a Question.
findings.reasoning: Type matters for estimation (strategic vs financial bidders). The filing states the split exactly, so Unknown discards reported information. The sort order puts two strategic bids after the deadline that governed them, which misstates the sequence (use 4). The price-range placement is the only part that depends on a convention.

findings.claim: The annexed merger agreement dates Insight's confidentiality agreement to 06/14/2016. The winner's entry therefore has a reported day, but the ledger leaves Insight inside the undated strategic NDA cohort.
findings.current_workbook: #16 (Excel row 17) '9 strategic NDA signers (incl. Insight, Party B)', Count 9, 'Execution dates not given', Date from 06/06/2016, Date to blank. There is no Insight NDA row.

evidence.quote: provisions of the Confidentiality Agreement dated June 14, 2016 between Parent and the Company
Beginning June 6, Raymond James contacted 13 strategic acquirers (including Party A, Party B and Insight)

rules: C3 (a fact found outside the background earns a row on the same test; quote that page and say where it comes from)
E7 (NDA signed dated at execution)
E3 Cohorts (members with their own rows are removed; the cohort holds the remainder, with the total in the Note)
findings.proposed_correction: Insert an 'NDA signed' row: Insight, Strategic, Process 1, Round 2, Count 1, When 06/14/2016, Sort/Date from/Date to 06/14/2016. Quote the Annex A §5.6(b) text (p. A-32), and say in the Note that the date comes from the merger agreement. Place it after #16 and before #17 (Sort 06/18). Reduce #16 to '8 strategic NDA signers (incl. Party B)', Count 8, with the Note giving the filing's total of 10 (Party A #7, Insight new row). Optionally set Date to on the Insight contact inside #15 no later than 06/14.
findings.reasoning: Use 1 and use 4: the winner's entry date fixes when it became a live bidder. It also shows that Insight was under an NDA before the 06/21–07/07 executive presentations (Insight's was 06/28). The information is in the supplied filing and the instruction requires reading the annexes.

findings.claim: Insight's 11/01 cut to $11.00 and its 11/02 agreement to $11.25 carry Conditions = Light. The support is diligence that finished later (11/02–11/06), but the narrative shows substantive diligence still open when each bid was made, and neither bid states a condition. Under E12 that is Unclear, not Light.
findings.current_workbook: #63 (Excel row 64) Conditions Light: 'no financing needed; remaining diligence completed 11/02–11/06'. #65 (Excel row 66) Light: 'diligence and documentation completed 11/02–11/06'. Q7 recommends keeping these.

evidence.quote: Insight would continue its due diligence
would like to conduct a detailed financial review of the third quarter results and expectations for the fourth quarter
Additional commercial and legal due diligence continued during this period as well.
Insight completed its due diligence investigation of the Company

rules: E12 (Light only for confirmatory/expedited/limited diligence or documentation; Unclear where the narrative shows diligence still open while the bid states no condition; later changes do not rewrite rows)
A ('Classify each offer ... as it stood at the time')
findings.proposed_correction: Set Conditions = Unclear on #63 and #65. Begin each Note with the driving fact, e.g. 'Unclear: diligence (commercial, legal, Q3/Q4 financial review) still open under the exclusivity to 11/07; no condition stated; no new financing needed.' Revise Q7. A reader could argue Heavy because the diligence ran inside a stated exclusive period, so state that alternative in Q7.
findings.reasoning: Use 3: the Conditions flag lets conditional formal bids be reinterpreted. When the bids were made, the filing shows ongoing commercial, legal and financial diligence. It never calls that diligence confirmatory. Completion four days later is hindsight, which Part A excludes. The Light label is also hard to square with the draft's own Heavy on Insight's 09/01 bid, which rested on a pending exclusive diligence period.

findings.claim: The 11/02 $11.25 bid row has All cash = Yes, justified by the later signed consideration. The bid as reported states only a dollar price, and Insight's other rows say Not stated.
findings.current_workbook: #65 (Excel row 66) All cash Yes; Note: 'Cash: this is the signed $11.25 cash consideration.'

evidence.quote: Mr. Lamneck agreed to the increased offer price of $11.25 per share
The merger consideration will be $11.25 per share in cash

rules: E13 ('A dollar price alone does not establish cash: use Not stated')
A (classify as it stood at the time)
findings.proposed_correction: Set All cash = Not stated on #65, as on #63 and Insight's earlier bids, and keep the cash consideration on #66 (signing).
findings.reasoning: The label is inconsistent within one bidder's sequence and rests on a later event. The research impact is small because signing four days later confirms cash.

findings.claim: The filing counts Party A's 03/29 proposal as one of the round-2 IOIs, and the Rounds sheet counts it among round-2 'Bids received' (10). The ledger has no round-2 row for Party A, however: its only priced rows are #9/#10 in round 1. The two sheets disagree, and nothing in the ledger records Party A as a round-2 bidder.
findings.current_workbook: Rounds round 1 'Bids received 1: Party A (03/29 ...)'. Rounds round 2 'Bids received 10 ... Party A's 03/29 proposal counted as its IOI'. The ledger has 9 round-2 bid units (#21, #22, #25, #26). #24 subtracts Party A as a submitter, and #30 (10 − 5 = 5) relies on it. No Question addresses how Party A's round-2 participation is represented; Q3 covers only its later status.

evidence.quote: Four strategic parties (in addition to Party A, which submitted the proposal described above on March 29, 2016), including Insight and Party B

rules: E6 ('A bid belongs to the solicitation it answers')
E10 (a new Bid row only for a change of price/terms; Bid reaffirmed only when finalizing)
F (Question for a call that could go either way and matters)
findings.proposed_correction: Raise a Question and choose one representation. (a) Add a round-2 'Other material event' on 07/27/2016 (Party A, Count 1): 'Target counts Party A's 03/29 proposal (#9/#10) as its round-2 IOI.' (b) Or make the Rounds line say '9 new IOIs plus Party A's round-1 proposal counted by the target'. Recommended: (a), so the ledger alone shows 10 round-2 bidder units.
findings.reasoning: Use 1 and use 2: the model reads round-2 competition and the 07/27 selection (top 5 of 10) from the ledger. Party A's valuation signal ($10.30–$10.75) either enters that selection or it does not. At present that depends on prose in the Rounds sheet. E10 bars a duplicate Bid row, and E6 assigns the bid to round 1, so this is a genuine convention gap and should not be fixed silently.

findings.claim: Party C's 10/04 reaffirmation of $11.25 is recorded as a new Bid, although nothing changed. Read literally, E10 creates a Bid row only for a change of price or material terms, and allows Bid reaffirmed only when the target is finalizing with that bidder, which it was not with Party C. Q2 recommends keeping the row, citing round accounting ('its only round-5 response'). That argument is not the E10 test.
findings.current_workbook: #55 (Excel row 56) Party C Bid $11.25, Formal, Heavy, round 5. Q2 recommends 'Keep as recorded'. #10 (Party A 04/12) is recorded the same way, although its 'substantially all' wording at least allows that something changed.

evidence.quote: On October 4, 2016, Party C reaffirmed its earlier offer of $11.25 per share.
requiring Insight, Party B and Party C to submit and affirm best and final acquisition proposals
Party A affirmed substantially all of these transaction terms, including the price per share

rules: E10 (Bid rows for changes; Bid reaffirmed only after target moves to finalize with the bidder and where it changes the record)
E6 (bid belongs to the solicitation it answers)
findings.proposed_correction: Keep Q2, but set out the literal E10 reading as the leading alternative. Under it, #55 becomes an 'Other material event' ('Party C confirms its $11.25 offer (#40) stands'), with no price, formality or conditions cells, and round 5 has no new Party C bid. Add the p.36 evidence ('submit and affirm best and final') to Q2. Keep #10 as a Bid only if the 'updated indication of interest' is read as changing terms, and say so.
findings.reasoning: Use 2: whether Party C 'bid' in round 5 changes that round's Bids received (2 vs 1) and the competition the model sees for Insight in October. The research team should decide this explicitly. The p.36 'affirm' language shows the target treated the October confirmations as part of the best-and-final process, which bears on the choice.

findings.claim: Party C's final exit is inferred from the 10/26 exclusivity, with Exit reason 'Not stated'. The filing, however, gives the target's reasons for sidelining Party C: on 10/20 it refused Party C the Q3/Q4 information because its price was lower and its closing less certain, and the 10/26 board repeated the point. Two readings are available: a reported 'Dropped by target' on 10/20 (refused the next stage), or an exit reason of 'Lower offer than rivals'. The 09/02 inferred drops of Party B and Party C likewise come after 09/01 board reasons that the filing reports.
findings.current_workbook: #62 (Excel row 63) Party C, Dropped by target, by 10/26/2016, Exit reason Not stated, Inferred Y. #58 records the 10/20 withholding only as an information-access event. #46/#47 have Exit reason Not stated. Q9 addresses whether the drops happened, not their reasons or date.

evidence.quote: Party C was not provided this financial information because its re-affirmed proposed price of $11.25 per share was less than the price of $12.00
Our board discussed Party C's lower proposed price of $11.25 per share and the greater certainty of closing offered by the Insight proposal.
the financing structure and third-party diligence requests proposed by Party B were problematic when compared with the Insight proposal

rules: E14 (Dropped by target includes refusing a participant the next stage; inferred exits take Exit reason Not stated; reported exits first)
B (an exit label or reason the filing does not establish)
findings.proposed_correction: Raise a Question, or extend Q9. For Party C, the alternative is 'Dropped by target' on 10/20/2016, reported rather than inferred, with Exit reason 'Lower offer than rivals' and a Note on the certainty-of-closing ground. If the inferred 10/26 exclusivity exit is kept, keep 'Not stated' as E14 requires, but put the p.33 reasons in the Note. Treat #46/#47 the same way (Party B: Terms or process; Party C: Lower offer than rivals) only if those drops are reclassified as reported.
findings.reasoning: Use 1: exit reasons carry valuation information, and here the filing supplies the target's reasons. E14's mechanical rule (inferred → Not stated) and its 'reported exits first' rule point different ways for 10/20. Whether withholding the Q3 data is an exclusion is a judgment call that E14 does not settle.

findings.claim: The draft opens round 1 on 01/29 as a bilateral stage with Party A. E6's opening rule lists the triggers 'in order', beginning with 'the first outreach wave'. The bilateral trigger is the last fallback. Read literally, that ordering puts round 1 at the 06/06 outreach and Party A's pre-June activity in round 0, which is Q1's alternative (i). The mid-March request for a written proposal is, however, a target solicitation, and that supports the draft.
findings.current_workbook: #5 Round opened 01/29/2016 (Inferred Y). The Rounds sheet has 5 rounds. Q1 recommends keeping this map and lists alternative (i).

evidence.quote: determined that our management should continue to pursue the opportunity with Party A
As we requested in mid-March 2016, on March 29, 2016, Party A provided a written proposal
On June 6, 2016, Raymond James began contacting potential strategic acquirers

rules: E6 Round 1 opening order; round 0 for earlier approaches and unsolicited proposals
E6 new round when the set changes
findings.proposed_correction: No silent change. In Q1, note that E6's priority wording favours alternative (i), and that the target-requested 03/29 proposal favours the draft. Let the research team decide. If (i) is adopted, #5–#11 move to round 0, #5 and the Rounds round-1 line are deleted, and rounds 2–5 become 1–4.
findings.reasoning: Use 2: this determines whether Party A's $10.30–$10.75 financing-contingent proposal is read as a response to a solicitation or as a preliminary approach. It also shifts every round number.

findings.claim: Insight's standing $12.00 offer gained new closing conditions: pre-closing pro forma 8-K adjustments and auditor consent. Insight made them a requirement for signing. The draft records this as an 'Other material event', so Insight's latest bid row (#44) still shows the pre-change conditions.
findings.current_workbook: #48 (Excel row 49) Other material event 'New condition ...'. #44 remains Insight's latest priced row (Formal, Heavy on exclusivity grounds).

evidence.quote: a provision requiring the receipt of the consent of our independent auditors
Insight would not be willing to enter into the merger agreement

rules: E10 (every change of price or material economic terms is its own Bid row)
E12 (Heavy: another material stated condition, such as an identified obstacle to completion)
findings.proposed_correction: Keep #48 as recorded, or recast it as an Insight Bid row at $12.00 ('conditions revised from #44'; Formal; Heavy: auditor-consent closing condition). The deciding question is whether a new closing condition counts as a 'material economic term'. Mention it in Q7.
findings.reasoning: Use 3: the conditions history of the winning bid is what makes reinterpretation possible. Conditions stays Heavy either way, so the effect on the data is small.

findings.claim: The projections section says the management Projections were given to Insight for its due diligence. It does not say whether Party B, Party C or other bidders received them. No ledger row or Note mentions this.
findings.current_workbook: No mention of the Projections being provided to Insight.

evidence.quote: The Projections were also provided to Insight in connection with its due diligence review of a possible transaction

rules: E2 (difference in information access earns a row wherever the filing reports it)
C1/C3 (read the projections section; facts outside the background)
findings.proposed_correction: No new row: the filing does not report a difference in access, only that Insight received them. Add a sentence to the Note of an Insight diligence row (e.g., #57), citing p.39, that Insight received the Projections and that other bidders' access is not stated.
findings.reasoning: This is uncertain. If other bidders did not receive the Projections, it is an information asymmetry that matters for use 5. The filing's silence does not establish that, so the fact belongs in a Note, not in an event row.
